personas.name: Late-night premium orderer
personas.description: A 29-year-old DashPass subscriber who orders 4-5 times per week, predominantly after 9 PM. She works long hours and treats food delivery as a stress-free dinner ritual, not a convenience trade-off. She has a narrow set of trusted restaurants — 3 or 4 she cycles through weekly — and almost never browses the full catalog. She pays the DashPass fee without blinking; zero-delivery-fee is a given she no longer consciously appreciates. Her biggest friction is rebuilding her order from scratch after a restaurant menu changes slightly. A one-tap reorder from her home screen would save her 90 seconds she doesn't have at 10 PM.
personas.jtbd: Get me back to my usual order from my usual restaurant with zero decisions.

personas.name: Promo-driven restaurant orderer
personas.description: A 34-year-old who orders 2-3 times per week, primarily from restaurants with active discounts or 'free item' promotions. Not a DashPass subscriber — evaluates delivery fee + discount per order. Rarely reorders; the promo is the draw, not the restaurant loyalty. Has a well-trained 'deals' filter he applies before even seeing the menu. A one-tap reorder doesn't solve his problem because the promo is usually gone by the time he'd reorder. He does use the checkout flow heavily — tends to compare 2-3 restaurants before committing.
personas.jtbd: Find the best deal available right now and get the food without hidden fees.

personas.name: Grocery stock-up orderer
personas.description: A 41-year-old who uses the app primarily for grocery and household item delivery — not restaurant orders. Places 1-2 large orders per week, almost always Saturday morning. The cart is complex: 15-25 items, mixing fresh produce, pantry staples, and cleaning supplies. She has a strong mental model of what she needs and dislikes the app pushing restaurant suggestions on the grocery home rail. Substitutions frustrate her most — when an item is out, the auto-substitute is often wrong and she has to edit post-delivery. Reorder is useful to her but at the grocery level ('reorder my weekly shop'), not the item level.
personas.jtbd: Get my weekly groceries delivered reliably on Saturday morning without substitution surprises.

personas.name: New user explorer
personas.description: A 23-year-old who installed the app 11 days ago and has completed 4 orders, all from different restaurants. Still building their mental model of the app — has explored the 'cuisine' filter twice, checked the tracking screen on every order, and left feedback (stars) on 3 out of 4 deliveries. Highly sensitive to first-order friction: a confusing checkout state or a missing promo code field nearly caused abandonment on order 2. Strongly influenced by 'popular' and 'top-rated' social signals. No strong reorder behavior yet — they're still in discovery mode.
personas.jtbd: Figure out which restaurants are worth ordering from and build a reliable go-to list.

personas.name: Lapsing disengaged user
personas.description: A 38-year-old who ordered 8-10 times per month six months ago but has placed only 1 order in the last 30 days. No clear precipitating event — prices crept up, a competing app ran a sign-up promo, and the habit just faded. Still has the app; gets push notifications but rarely opens them. Not a DashPass subscriber since the subscription lapsed two months ago. Unlikely to reorder even if prompted — the activation energy to remember why they liked the app in the first place is too high. Price sensitivity is the main lever.
personas.jtbd: Honestly, I'd need a strong reason to go back to ordering regularly.

personas.name: Speed-first pragmatist
personas.description: A 31-year-old who places 3-4 orders per week, always from restaurants with under 30-minute estimated delivery. Never browses; goes straight to search, types a cuisine or dish, filters by ETA, and orders the first result that has >4 stars and no minimum above $12. Has abandoned the checkout flow twice when the total exceeded expectations at the confirmation step. A DashPass subscriber, but primarily for the delivery fee savings on quick orders — would cancel if the benefit didn't materially cut the total. Reorder works for him but only for the same-day use case ('I ordered from here Tuesday, it was fast, I want it again now').
personas.jtbd: Get good food from somewhere fast — I don't want to spend more than 2 minutes deciding.
